observation: Round 1 moved the proxy down (0.648 -> 0.607) while doing exactly what was intended on the far rings and over-shooting in the dense centre. Wins: det_real_detection_ratio 0.8 -> 0.9, ring 2 (x~363) now has a real oblique pair (red x~150-230 y~1070, green x~190-220 y~1300) giving a K midpoint at y=1180 that is phase-consistent with the stagger; sam_ontology_divergence fell 0.240 -> 0.187 and sam_segment_size_cv 1.34 -> 1.18; ring count still 10/10 and the vertical guard held. Loss: in detected_lines.png the relaxed oblique path now also fires on the regularly spaced bolt-hole rows inside the K/A blocks of the near-scanner rings (new obliques at y~1200, ~1400, ~1650, ~1800-1900, ~2270, ~2600), i.e. features that are NOT K-block edges (K edges are at ~1072/1288 and ~1497/1713). For ring 6 (x~1330) a spurious positive/negative pair produced a midpoint at y=1438, mid-way between the two stagger rows; segmentation_results.png shows that ring's K block sitting between rows, and det_y_std jumped to 204 px. Those extra unexplained joint lines plus the mis-phased ring cut correspondence_f1@15 from 0.368 to 0.290 (precision loss dominates). Fill rate and NaN were essentially unchanged (0.726, 0.101), so stages 1-3 remain healthy and the regression is purely a detection precision problem.
rule: d9 / f_spurious_lines (prompt-relevant lines much more numerous than the K-edge set) with the classic maxLineGap mechanism: bolt-hole features spaced ~50-60 px apart get bridged into pseudo-obliques once maxLineGap exceeds their spacing, and a lower binary threshold lets those shallow features into the binarised map. Remediation r_tighten_hough, but applied selectively: shrink maxLineGap_oblique below the bolt-hole pitch and restore the binarisation depth cut, while keeping the two changes that plausibly delivered the ring-2 detection (denser joint interpolation via inter_radius and the lower oblique accumulator threshold, which accepts the short but genuine far-ring K edges). Keep r_tighten_hough on horizontal and the vertical guard since 10/10 verticals held.
failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_spurious_lines (bolt-hole rows bridged into oblique lines in the near-scanner rings) -> stage_5_segmentation.f_crop_offset on ring 6 (K midpoint at 1438 instead of the 1180/1605 stagger rows); the underlying stage-3 f_joint_oversmoothed on far rings is partially fixed and should be preserved.
rationale: Disentangle the two effects of round 1: keep the recall-side changes that rescued ring 2 (enhancing.inter_radius 0.075, hough_threshold_oblique 42) and reverse the precision-side changes that created the spurious centre obliques. maxLineGap_oblique goes from 60 to 30 (below the anchor's 40 and below the ~50-60 px bolt-hole pitch) so dashed feature rows can no longer be fused into lines while genuine, continuous K joints (now densified by the larger inter_radius) still pass; binary_threshold goes back to 130 (slightly above the 127 default) so shallow intra-block features are cut before Hough. hough_threshold_horizontal stays 60 and hough_threshold_vertical stays 560 - both behaved (no spurious horizontal prompts, 10/10 verticals). Denoising untouched; SAM untouched; unfolding omitted (stage1 locked). Expected: the number of unexplained (orange) joint lines drops back to or below anchor level, ring 6 returns to the 1605 row (det_y_std back to ~210 -> two-row pattern, midpoint ratio stays high), ring 2 keeps its real detection, so correspondence_f1@15 should exceed the anchor's 0.368 rather than merely recover it; ring_count_error must stay 0.
